skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // PhysMemoryManager - Specifications
5. //
6. // This file contains specification functions and view types.
7. 
8. verus! {
9. 
10. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
11. use vstd::map::*;
12. 
13. pub uninterp spec fn byte_at_address(ptr: int) -> u8;
14. 
15. /// Abstract view of the frame allocator (`frame::Inner`).
16. ///
17. /// Captures which physical frames are currently allocated vs. free,
18. /// together with a per-frame reference count that models shared
19. /// ownership (e.g. copy-on-write after `share()`).
20. pub struct FrameAllocView
21. {
22.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,
23.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,
24.     /// Maps each allocated frame address to its reference count.
25.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated.
26.     pub refcounts: Map<int, int>,
27. }
28. 
29. impl FrameAllocView
30. {
31.     pub open spec fn wf(&self) -> bool
32.     {
33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
35.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
36.         // Disjoint
37.         &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
44.         // Refcount bounded by u8 range
45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
46.             0 < self.refcounts[addr] <= 255
47.     }
48. }
49. 
50. //==================================================================================================
51. // LinkedList — external type registration
52. //==================================================================================================
53. //
54. // `vstd` provides no specification for `alloc::collections::LinkedList`, so it must be
55. // registered as an external type before it can appear in spec signatures. Only the type
56. // is registered here; no `View`/iterator specification is provided, because the orphan
57. // rule forbids a downstream crate from implementing vstd's `View` / `ForLoopGhostIterator`
58. // traits for the foreign `LinkedList` / `linked_list::Iter` types. As a consequence, the
59. // two helpers that iterate a `LinkedList` in a `for` loop (`book_physical_memory_regions`,
60. // `book_mmio_regions`) cannot have their bodies verified and are `external_body`. See
61. // `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-mod/bugs.md`.
62. 
63. use ::core::alloc::Allocator;
64. 
65. #[verifier::external_type_specification]
66. #[verifier::external_body]
67. #[verifier::accept_recursive_types(T)]
68. #[verifier::reject_recursive_types(A)]
69. pub struct ExLinkedList<T, A: Allocator>(::alloc::collections::LinkedList<T, A>);
70. 
71. //==================================================================================================
72. // Physical-memory subsystem view
73. //==================================================================================================
74. 
75. /// Abstract view of the global physical-memory subsystem managed by `mm::phys`.
76. ///
77. /// Pure ghost description — names no `MaybeUninit`, `AtomicBool`, bitmap, refcount slice,
78. /// or any other storage mechanism. It wraps the existing frame-allocator view
79. /// (`FrameAllocView`) with the two liveness facts the caller depends on.
80. pub ghost struct PhysModView {
81.     /// The frame allocator singleton has been initialized (`frame::init` ran
82.     /// successfully). All `frames`-related guarantees are meaningful only when this holds.
83.     pub initialized: bool,
84.     /// Abstract frame-allocator state: which physical frames are allocated (reserved) vs.
85.     /// free, with per-frame refcounts. This is the existing `FrameAllocView`.
86.     pub frames: FrameAllocView,
87.     /// The `PhysMemoryManager` singleton has been initialized with a fresh user page pool.
88.     pub manager_ready: bool,
89. }
90. 
91. /// Current abstract state of the global physical-memory subsystem.
92. ///
93. /// Uninterpreted accessor: the subsystem state lives in module-level singletons
94. /// (`frame::INSTANCE`/`INSTANCE_INIT` and the `PhysMemoryManager`/`Upool` singletons)
95. /// whose value is not directly spec-readable. The cross-call transition (`v -> v'`) is
96. /// realized in the proving phase by a ghost token over those singletons (see
97. /// `view_design.md` section 8); during the specification phase it is read like `self@`.
98. pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysModView;
99. 
100. impl PhysModView {
101.     /// Well-formedness invariant of the subsystem.
102.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
103.         // Once the allocator is up, the frame partition is well formed.
104.         &&& self.initialized ==> self.frames.wf()
105.         // The manager layer can only be up if the allocator is up.
106.         &&& self.manager_ready ==> self.initialized
107.     }
108. 
109.     /// The subsystem is fully brought up and self-consistent.
110.     pub open spec fn live(self) -> bool {
111.         &&& self.initialized
112.         &&& self.manager_ready
113.         &&& self.frames.wf()
114.     }
115. }
116. 
117. //==================================================================================================
118. // Frame-set vocabulary (on the existing FrameAllocView)
119. //==================================================================================================
120. 
121. impl FrameAllocView {
122.     /// The allocator tracks (covers) the frame at `addr` — it is one of the frames this
123.     /// allocator knows about, allocated or free. Models `frame::is_covered`.
124.     pub open spec fn covers(self, addr: int) -> bool {
125.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) || self.free_frames.contains(addr)
126.     }
127. 
128.     /// The frame at `addr` is reserved: present in the allocated set, hence `alloc()` can
129.     /// never return it. This is the core caller-visible fact a "booked" frame satisfies.
130.     pub open spec fn reserved(self, addr: int) -> bool {
131.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr)
132.     }
133. 
134.     /// Every frame address in `set` is reserved.
135.     pub open spec fn all_reserved(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
136.         forall|a: int| set.contains(a) ==> self.reserved(a)
137.     }
138. 
139.     /// Every frame address in `set` is currently free (booking precondition: a range can be
140.     /// booked only if it is entirely free).
141.     pub open spec fn all_free(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
142.         forall|a: int| #[trigger] set.contains(a) ==> self.free_frames.contains(a)
143.     }
144. 
145.     /// Reserve every frame in `set` (each assumed free in `self`): move it from
146.     /// `free_frames` to `allocated_frames` with refcount 1.
147.     pub open spec fn book_all(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
148.         FrameAllocView {
149.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.union(set),
150.             free_frames: self.free_frames.difference(set),
151.             refcounts: self.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
152.                 Map::new(|a: int| set.contains(a), |a: int| 1int),
153.             ),
154.         }
155.     }
156. 
157.     /// Reserve only the *covered* frames of `set`; skip the rest (coverage-gated). Models
158.     /// the MMIO booking rule.
159.     pub open spec fn book_covered(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
160.         self.book_all(set.filter(|a: int| self.covers(a)))
161.     }
162. }
163. 
164. /// Page-aligned physical frame addresses covered by a region `[start, start + size)`.
165. /// Mirrors the frame-set computation used by `frame::alloc_range`.
166. pub open spec fn region_frame_addrs(start: int, size: int) -> Set<int> {
167.     let start_frame_number = start / spec_page_size();
168.     let end_frame_number = (start + size) / spec_page_size();
169.     vstd::set_lib::set_int_range(start_frame_number, end_frame_number)
170.         .map(|i: int| i * spec_page_size())
171. }
172. 
173. /// The set of physical frame addresses covered by all regions in a physical
174. /// non-usable-memory list. Uninterpreted: `LinkedList` has no Verus model, so its contents
175. /// cannot be folded over in spec; this names the abstract union of `region_frame_addrs`
176. /// over the list, which is all the contract needs.
177. pub uninterp spec fn phys_regions_frame_set(
178.     regions: &::alloc::collections::LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
179. ) -> Set<int>;
180. 
181. /// The set of physical frame addresses covered by all MMIO regions in a list (after
182. /// GVA->GPA translation). Uninterpreted for the same reason as `phys_regions_frame_set`.
183. pub uninterp spec fn mmio_regions_frame_set(
184.     regions: &::alloc::collections::LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
185. ) -> Set<int>;
186. 
187. } // end verus!
188. 
189.

1. verus! {
2. 
3. /// After `frame::init` succeeds, the frame allocator singleton is initialized and its
4. /// abstract partition is well formed.
5. ///
6. /// `frame::init` is `external_body`, so this fact is asserted as a lemma over the global
7. /// `phys_view()` accessor rather than derived from the exec body. The proving phase will
8. /// discharge it against the frame-allocator initialization contract.
9. pub proof fn lemma_frame_initialized()
10.     ensures
11.         phys_view().initialized,
12.         phys_view().frames.wf(),
13. {
14.     admit();
15. }
16. 
17. /// After `PhysMemoryManager::init` succeeds, the manager layer is ready.
18. ///
19. /// `PhysMemoryManager::init` is `external_body`, so this fact is asserted as a lemma over
20. /// the global `phys_view()` accessor. The proving phase will discharge it against the
21. /// manager initialization contract.
22. pub proof fn lemma_manager_ready()
23.     ensures
24.         phys_view().manager_ready,
25. {
26.     admit();
27. }
28. 
29. } // end verus!
30.

1. # Bugs — mm::phys
2. 
3. ## Code bugs
4. 
5. None found. The three target functions (`init`, `book_physical_memory_regions`,
6. `book_mmio_regions`) are logically correct; no overflow, off-by-one, or impossible
7. path was detected during speccing.
8. 
9. ## Verifier limitation (not a code bug) — LinkedList iteration
10. 
11. **What**: `book_physical_memory_regions` and `book_mmio_regions` iterate an
12. `alloc::collections::LinkedList` with a `for region in list.iter()` loop. Verus
13. cannot reason about either function's body.
14. 
15. **Why**: `vstd` ships no specification for `LinkedList`. Supporting a `for` loop over
16. `list.iter()` requires implementing vstd's `View`, `ForLoopGhostIteratorNew`, and
17. `ForLoopGhostIterator` traits for the foreign `LinkedList` / `linked_list::Iter`
18. types. Rust's orphan rule (E0117) forbids a downstream crate (the kernel) from
19. implementing vstd-owned traits for std-owned types — only `vstd` itself may do so,
20. and the pinned toolchain `vstd` does not. Registering the type alone
21. (`external_type_specification`, done in `mod.spec.rs` as `ExLinkedList`) lets the type
22. appear in spec signatures but does not provide iteration semantics.
23. 
24. **Consequence / deviation**: both helpers are marked `#[verus_verify(external_body)]`
25. with meaningful `requires`/`ensures` describing their effect on the abstract
26. `phys_view()` (every physical region frame becomes reserved; every *covered* MMIO frame
27. becomes reserved, uncovered skipped). They are listed in `tcb-allowed.md`. `init` itself
28. has no loop and **is** body-verified, calling the two helpers through their contracts.
29. 
30. **Resolution path**: if/when `vstd` gains a `LinkedList` model (or these lists are
31. replaced by `Vec`/`VecDeque`, which `vstd` already supports), the `external_body`
32. markers can be removed and the loop bodies verified directly.
33. 
34. **How Verus helped**: surfaced that the data structure choice (`LinkedList`) is opaque
35. to verification; a `Vec`/`VecDeque` would be fully verifiable here.
36.

 None found. The three target functions (`init`, `book_physical_memory_regions`,
 `book_mmio_regions`) are logically correct; no overflow, off-by-one, or impossible
 path was detected during speccing.
 
 ## Verifier limitation (not a code bug) — LinkedList iteration
 
 **What**: `book_physical_memory_regions` and `book_mmio_regions` iterate an
 `alloc::collections::LinkedList` with a `for region in list.iter()` loop. Verus
 cannot reason about either function's body.
 
 **Why**: `vstd` ships no specification for `LinkedList`. Supporting a `for` loop over
 `list.iter()` requires implementing vstd's `View`, `ForLoopGhostIteratorNew`, and
 `ForLoopGhostIterator` traits for the foreign `LinkedList` / `linked_list::Iter`
 types. Rust's orphan rule (E0117) forbids a downstream crate (the kernel) from
 implementing vstd-owned traits for std-owned types — only `vstd` itself may do so,
 and the pinned toolchain `vstd` does not. Registering the type alone
 (`external_type_specification`, done in `mod.spec.rs` as `ExLinkedList`) lets the type
 appear in spec signatures but does not provide iteration semantics.
 
 **Consequence / deviation**: both helpers are marked `#[verus_verify(external_body)]`
 with meaningful `requires`/`ensures` describing their effect on the abstract
 `phys_view()` (every physical region frame becomes reserved; every *covered* MMIO frame
 becomes reserved, uncovered skipped). They are listed in `tcb-allowed.md`. `init` itself
 has no loop and **is** body-verified, calling the two helpers through their contracts.
 
 **Resolution path**: if/when `vstd` gains a `LinkedList` model (or these lists are
 replaced by `Vec`/`VecDeque`, which `vstd` already supports), the `external_body`
 markers can be removed and the loop bodies verified directly.
 
 **How Verus helped**: surfaced that the data structure choice (`LinkedList`) is opaque
 to verification; a `Vec`/`VecDeque` would be fully verifiable here.

3. > Phase output. Designs the abstract `View` that all later specs
4. > (`requires`/`ensures`) for `init`, `book_physical_memory_regions`, and
5. > `book_mmio_regions` will reference.
6. >

8. > (`body_removed_source.rs`), plus the **existing, do-not-modify** spec
9. > definitions (`byte_at_address`, `FrameAllocView`, `FrameAllocView::wf`,

11. >
12. > Target functions in scope: `init`, `book_physical_memory_regions`,
13. > `book_mmio_regions`. (`test` is out of scope.)
14. 
15. ---
16. 
17. ## 1. Abstract Resource (from caller analysis)
18. 
19. `mm::phys` is, to its one caller (`kernel_vas::init`), the **boot-time
20. constructor of the machine's global physical-memory subsystem**. After
21. `init(..) -> Ok(())` the caller depends on a *world* in which:
22. 
23. 1. the **global frame allocator singleton is live** (initialized exactly once
24.    from the firmware bitmap) and internally consistent;
25. 2. every frame of every supplied *non-usable* physical region has been
26.    **reserved** (booked) — moved out of the free pool so a later `alloc()`
27.    can never hand it out;
28. 3. every **tracked** MMIO frame has been reserved, while MMIO frames the
29.    allocator does *not* track are **silently skipped** (coverage-gated);
30. 4. the **`PhysMemoryManager` singleton + a fresh user page pool are live**
31.    (the layer the rest of boot builds on);
32. 5. the whole thing satisfies the frame-allocator well-formedness
33.    `FrameAllocView::wf` (free/allocated disjoint, page-aligned,
34.    refcount-consistent).
35. 
36. `init` is the *only* externally observed function; `book_*` are private
37. helpers reachable only through `init`, so their contracts exist purely to
38. support `init`'s post-state. The caller observes **only `Ok(())` vs `Err`** —
39. never a partial state, never the iteration order, never the `Error` variant,
40. never whether MMIO is walked per-page.
41. 
42. These three functions are **free functions over global singletons**
43. (`frame::INSTANCE` + `frame::INSTANCE_INIT`, and the `PhysMemoryManager` /
44. `Upool` singletons), not `&mut self` methods. The View therefore models the
45. **abstract state of that global subsystem**, and the `v -> v'` transitions are
46. realized in the proof phase by a ghost token over the singletons (see §8) —
47. exactly as the bump-allocator View deferred its atomic-ghost token.
48. 
49. ---
50. 
51. ## 2. The View
52. 
53. The only abstract state these functions establish or mutate is: *is the
54. subsystem up*, *which physical frames are reserved vs. free*, and *is the
55. manager layer up*. The frame partition is **already** captured by the
56. do-not-modify `FrameAllocView` (the `View for Inner`). The phys-mod View wraps
57. it and adds the two liveness facts the caller depends on.

59. ```rust
60. /// Abstract view of the global physical-memory subsystem managed by
61. /// `mm::phys`. Pure ghost description — names no `MaybeUninit`, `AtomicBool`,
62. /// bitmap, refcount slice, or any other storage mechanism.
63. pub ghost struct PhysModView {
64.     /// The frame allocator singleton has been initialized (`frame::init` ran
65.     /// successfully). All `frames`-related guarantees are meaningful only
66.     /// when this holds.
67.     pub initialized: bool,
68.     /// Abstract frame-allocator state: which physical frames are allocated
69.     /// (reserved) vs. free, with per-frame refcounts. This is the existing,
70.     /// do-not-modify `FrameAllocView` (== the `View for Inner` of the global
71.     /// `frame::INSTANCE`).
72.     pub frames: FrameAllocView,
73.     /// The `PhysMemoryManager` singleton has been initialized with a fresh
74.     /// user page pool (`Upool`). A single liveness bit — the caller observes
75.     /// only that this layer is up, never its contents.
76.     pub manager_ready: bool,
77. }
78. ```
79. 
80. Attachment (no struct in `mod.rs` to `impl View` for; the state is global):
81. 
82. ```rust
83. /// Current abstract state of the global physical-memory subsystem.
84. /// Uninterpreted accessor; the proof phase pins it to the frame /
85. /// manager singletons via a ghost token (§8).
86. pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysModView;
87. ```
88. 
89. `phys_view()` is read by specs exactly like `self@` would be: `init`'s ensures
90. talk about `phys_view()` before vs. after the call.
91. 
92. ### 2.1 Derived spec helpers
93. 
94. Reusable frame-set vocabulary lives **on `FrameAllocView`** (a *new* `impl`
95. block — the existing `struct`/`wf` are untouched), so every spec speaks the
96. same language:
97. 
98. ```rust
99. impl FrameAllocView {
100.     /// The allocator tracks (covers) the frame at `addr` — it is one of the
101.     /// frames this allocator knows about, allocated or free. Models
102.     /// `frame::is_covered`.
103.     pub open spec fn covers(self, addr: int) -> bool {
104.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) || self.free_frames.contains(addr)
105.     }
106. 
107.     /// The frame at `addr` is reserved: present in the allocated set, hence
108.     /// `alloc()` can never return it. This is the core caller-visible fact a
109.     /// "booked" frame satisfies.
110.     pub open spec fn reserved(self, addr: int) -> bool {
111.         self.allocated_frames.contains(addr)
112.     }
113. 
114.     /// Every frame address in `set` is reserved.
115.     pub open spec fn all_reserved(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
116.         forall|a: int| set.contains(a) ==> self.reserved(a)
117.     }
118. 
119.     /// Every frame address in `set` is currently free (booking precondition:
120.     /// a range can be booked only if it is entirely free).
121.     pub open spec fn all_free(self, set: Set<int>) -> bool {
122.         forall|a: int| set.contains(a) ==> self.free_frames.contains(a)
123.     }
124. }
125. ```
126. 
127. Region → frame-set bridge (defined over the public region accessors
128. `start()`/`size()`; exact closed form finalized in the spec phase):
129. 
130. ```rust
131. /// The set of page-aligned physical frame addresses covered by a physical
132. /// memory region `[start, start + size)`. Uses the existing `frame_addr_of`.
133. pub open spec fn region_frames(start_frame: int, num_frames: int) -> Set<int> {
134.     Set::new(|a: int| exists|i: int|
135.         0 <= i < num_frames && a == frame_addr_of(start_frame + i))
136. }
137. ```
138. 
139. PhysModView convenience predicate used in `init`'s post-state:
140. 
141. ```rust
142. impl PhysModView {
143.     /// The subsystem is fully brought up and self-consistent.
144.     pub open spec fn live(self) -> bool {
145.         self.initialized && self.manager_ready && self.frames.wf()
146.     }
147. }
148. ```
149. 
150. ---
151. 
152. ## 3. Well-formedness Invariant `inv()`
153. 
154. ```rust
155. impl PhysModView {
156.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
157.         // (a) Once the allocator is up, the frame partition is well formed.
158.         //     `FrameAllocView::wf` = free/allocated disjoint, page-aligned,
159.         //     refcount/allocated consistency, refcounts in 1..=255.
160.         &&& self.initialized ==> self.frames.wf()
161.         // (b) The manager layer is built on top of the frame allocator, so it
162.         //     can only be up if the allocator is up.
163.         &&& self.manager_ready ==> self.initialized
164.     }
165. }
166. ```
167. 
168. | Clause | Guarantees caller invariant |
169. |--------|-----------------------------|
170. | (a) `initialized ==> frames.wf()` | the downstream-relied-upon consistency (disjoint, aligned, refcount-consistent) holds whenever the allocator is live |
171. | (b) `manager_ready ==> initialized` | the manager singleton is never "up" over a dead allocator — rejects an init that builds the manager without seeding frames |
172. 
173. `inv()` is deliberately thin: the heavy lifting (`wf`) is reused from the
174. existing frame View, and the two implications encode the only ordering
175. constraint between the two liveness bits.
176. 
177. ---
178. 
179. ## 4. Spec transitions of the target functions
180. 
181. State is `v = phys_view()` (pre), `v' = phys_view()` (post). All clauses are
182. stated only over `PhysModView` / `FrameAllocView`; nothing names the
183. singleton storage.
184. 
185. ### 4.1 Frame-set transitions (on `FrameAllocView`)
186. 
187. ```rust
188. impl FrameAllocView {
189.     /// Reserve a single currently-free frame: move it from `free_frames` to
190.     /// `allocated_frames` with refcount 1. (Models `frame::book` /
191.     /// per-frame effect of `alloc_range` on a covered, free frame.)
192.     pub open spec fn book_frame(self, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
193.         FrameAllocView {
194.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
195.             free_frames: self.free_frames.remove(addr),
196.             refcounts: self.refcounts.insert(addr, 1),
197.         }
198.     }
199. 
200.     /// Reserve every frame in `set` (each must be free in `self`).
201.     /// Used to describe `alloc_range` over a region's frames.
202.     pub open spec fn book_all(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
203.         FrameAllocView {
204.             allocated_frames: self.allocated_frames.union(set),
205.             free_frames: self.free_frames.difference(set),
206.             refcounts: Map::new(
207.                 |a: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(a) || set.contains(a),
208.                 |a: int| if set.contains(a) { 1 } else { self.refcounts[a] }),
209.         }
210.     }
211. 
212.     /// Reserve only the *covered* frames of `set`; skip the rest (coverage-
213.     /// gated). Models the MMIO booking rule.
214.     pub open spec fn book_covered(self, set: Set<int>) -> FrameAllocView {
215.         self.book_all(set.filter(|a: int| self.covers(a)))
216.     }
217. }
218. ```
219. 
220. ### 4.2 `book_physical_memory_regions(regions) -> Result<(), Error>`
221. 
222. Private; called once by `init`. Consumes the list by value. Let `R` be the
223. union of `region_frames(..)` over all regions in the list.
224. 
225. ```
226. requires  v.inv() && v.initialized          // allocator must be live first
227. 
228. ensures   v'.inv() && v'.initialized && v'.manager_ready == v.manager_ready
229. 
230.           match result {
231.             Ok(()) => {
232.               // every region was entirely free, and is now entirely reserved
233.               &&& v.frames.all_free(R)
234.               &&& v'.frames == v.frames.book_all(R)     // hence v'.frames.all_reserved(R)
235.             }
236.             Err(_) => {
237.               // fail-fast on a booking conflict: some region was NOT free.
238.               // Booking stops at the first failing region; earlier regions
239.               // stay booked, so the partition is still well formed but only a
240.               // prefix is reserved. No in-scope caller observes this state.
241.               &&& !v.frames.all_free(R)
242.               &&& v'.frames.wf()
243.             }
244.           }
245. ```
246. 
247. Error condition is stated as one **abstract interface predicate**
248. (`!all_free(R)` ⇔ a conflict with an already-reserved frame), not as a list of
249. code checks — this is the "fail-fast on conflict" property the caller relies on.
250. 
251. ### 4.3 `book_mmio_regions(&regions) -> Result<(), Error>`
252. 
253. Private; called once by `init`. Borrows the list. Let `M` be the union of
254. `region_frames(..)` over the MMIO regions (after GVA→GPA translation; the
255. translation is total on the success path).
256. 
257. ```
258. requires  v.inv() && v.initialized
259. 
260. ensures   v'.inv() && v'.initialized && v'.manager_ready == v.manager_ready
261. 
262.           match result {
263.             Ok(()) => {
264.               // tracked MMIO frames booked; untracked ones skipped, untouched.
265.               &&& v'.frames == v.frames.book_covered(M)
266.               // ⇒ forall f in M: v.frames.covers(f) ==> v'.frames.reserved(f)
267.               // ⇒ forall f in M: !v.frames.covers(f) ==> frame state unchanged
268.             }
269.             Err(_) => {
270.               // a covered frame was already reserved (book conflict) or an
271.               // address conversion failed; partition stays well formed.
272.               &&& v'.frames.wf()
273.             }
274.           }
275. ```
276. 
277. The `Ok` arm makes the coverage gate explicit and surfaces both halves the
278. caller depends on: covered ⇒ reserved, **and** uncovered ⇒ *not* assumed
279. reserved (state unchanged for those frames).
280. 
281. ### 4.4 `init(physical_memory_regions, &mmio_regions, physical_memory_layout) -> Result<(), Error>`
282. 
283. The only public function. Let `P` = union of `region_frames` over
284. `physical_memory_regions`, `M` = union over `mmio_regions`. `seed(bitmap)` is
285. the `FrameAllocView` produced by `frame::init` from the bitmap (frames it
286. tracks, partitioned per the bitmap's set bits).
287. 
288. ```
289. requires  v.inv()
290.           !v.initialized            // one-shot: frame allocator not yet up
291.                                      // (frame::init rejects a second call)
292. 
293. ensures   v'.inv()
294. 
295.           match result {
296.             Ok(()) => {
297.               // (1) subsystem fully live & consistent
298.               &&& v'.live()                          // initialized && manager_ready && frames.wf()
299.               // (2) seeded from the bitmap, then phys regions booked, then
300.               //     covered MMIO frames booked
301.               &&& v'.frames == seed(physical_memory_layout@)
302.                                    .book_all(P)
303.                                    .book_covered(M)
304.               // (3) booked ⇒ never allocated (the core safety property)
305.               &&& v'.frames.all_reserved(P)
306.               &&& forall|f: int| M.contains(f) && v'.frames.covers(f)
307.                       ==> v'.frames.reserved(f)
308.             }
309.             Err(_) => {
310.               // boot aborts; caller uses `?` and never touches the subsystem
311.               // again. No partial-state guarantee is promised beyond inv().
312.               true
313.             }
314.           }
315. ```
316. 
317. Notes:
318. - (1) `v'.live()` is the single fact downstream `virt::init` / page-table
319.   setup needs (both singletons up, `wf` holds). It rejects a buggy `init`
320.   that returns `Ok` while leaving a singleton uninitialized.
321. - (3) is the headline caller property ("booked ⇒ never allocated"); it is
322.   *derivable* from (2) (`book_all`/`book_covered` definitions) but surfaced
323.   directly because it is exactly what the caller writes into its proof.
324. - The `Err` arm is intentionally `true` (only `inv()` is promised): the caller
325.   aborts on `?` and the analysis states no in-scope caller observes any
326.   particular partial state. Strengthening it would over-specify an
327.   unobserved, non-transactional path.
328. 
329. ---
330. 
331. ## 5. Substitution test (per field)
332. 
333. > *"If `mm::phys` / the frame allocator were rewritten with a different
334. > algorithm (e.g. a buddy allocator, a free-list, a different singleton
335. > mechanism), would this field still make sense?"*
336. 
337. | Field | Survives? | Reasoning |
338. |-------|-----------|-----------|
339. | `initialized` | ✅ | "Is the physical-memory subsystem up?" is observable regardless of how the singleton is stored (`AtomicBool`, `OnceCell`, …). The caller depends on exactly this one-shot liveness. |
340. | `frames: FrameAllocView` | ✅ | The free/allocated/refcount partition is the abstract resource *any* frame allocator maintains; it is the existing `View for Inner`. A buddy/free-list rewrite still exposes the same `Set<int>` partition. Names no bitmap/refcount-slice. |
341. | `manager_ready` | ✅ | "Is the `PhysMemoryManager` + user page pool layer up?" is a caller-observable liveness bit independent of how the manager is built. A single bool — the caller observes liveness, never contents. |
342. 
343. Every field describes the **subsystem's observable state**, not a mechanism.
344. The implementation's `MaybeUninit<Inner>`, `AtomicBool`, `Bitmap`, and
345. `[u8; NFRAMES]` refcount storage are *one* realization; the View commits to
346. none of them.
347. 
348. Helper predicates pass too: `covers`/`reserved`/`book_*` are phrased over the
349. abstract frame sets (`is_covered` = "tracked", `book` = "move free→allocated"),
350. all algorithm-independent.
351. 
352. ---
353. 
354. ## 6. Design rationale
355. 
356. - **Reuse, don't re-derive, the frame partition.** `FrameAllocView` already is
357.   the correct abstract state for the allocator and is shared with the
358.   `frame` submodule's verified `View for Inner`. Embedding it (rather than
359.   re-modeling frames) keeps `init`/`book_*` specs interoperable with the
360.   frame-level contracts they call (`frame::book`, `frame::alloc_range`,
361.   `frame::is_covered`) and honors the do-not-modify constraint.
362. - **Two liveness bits, nothing more.** The caller's *additional* observations
363.   beyond the frame partition are exactly "allocator up" and "manager up". Each
364.   is a single bool, each is used (`initialized` gates `book_*` preconditions
365.   and `frames.wf()`; `manager_ready` appears in `init`'s `live()`
366.   post-state). Minimal and complete.
367. - **Coverage-gating modeled as a `filter`.** `book_covered = book_all ∘
368.   filter(covers)` makes "tracked ⇒ booked, untracked ⇒ skipped" one
369.   declarative line, capturing the LAPIC-above-RAM skip the caller is warned
370.   about — without walking GVA→GPA per page.
371. - **Reserve-set vocabulary on the View.** `reserved`/`all_reserved`/`all_free`
372.   + `region_frames` turn "booked ⇒ never allocated" and the booking
373.   precondition into reusable predicates, so each ensures is a clause a caller
374.   drops straight into a proof.
375. - **Error paths fold to `inv()` (+ a conflict predicate).** Booking is
376.   non-transactional (partial on failure) and no in-scope caller observes the
377.   partial state, so the honest contract is: `Err` preserves `wf` and (for
378.   `book_physical_memory_regions`) reveals the abstract conflict condition
379.   `!all_free(R)`. We do **not** fabricate state-preservation that the code
380.   does not provide.
381. - **`init` post-state as a composed transition.** `seed(..).book_all(P)
382.   .book_covered(M)` is a single declarative description of the whole boot
383.   sequence; the headline safety fact (3) is surfaced separately because that
384.   is the form the caller actually uses.
385. 
386. ---
387. 
388. ## 7. Rejected alternatives
389. 
390. 1. **No phys-mod View; specs reference `FrameAllocView` (and the raw global)
391.    directly.** Rejected. The frame partition alone cannot express "the
392.    allocator is initialized" (one-shot `init` precondition) or "the manager
393.    layer is up" — both are caller-observed. A thin wrapper carrying the two
394.    liveness bits is the minimal honest model.
395. 
396. 2. **Mirror the implementation: fields `instance_init: bool`,
397.    `bitmap: Seq<bool>`, `refcount: Seq<u8>`.** Rejected. Leaks the
398.    `AtomicBool` + `Bitmap` + refcount-slice mechanism, fails the substitution
399.    test (a buddy/free-list rewrite has no bitmap), and duplicates state the
400.    existing `FrameAllocView` already abstracts.
401. 
402. 3. **Model the manager/Upool with a full sub-View
403.    (`manager: PhysMemoryManagerView`).** Rejected for *this* module. The
404.    in-scope functions only need "manager up" (one bit); the caller observes
405.    only liveness here. A structured manager View belongs to the `manager`
406.    module's own verification, not phys-mod, and would require reading its
407.    internals (forbidden, and unnecessary). Promote to a sub-View later only if
408.    a caller is shown to depend on manager contents.
409. 
410. 4. **Track per-region booking results / fault flags in the View.** Rejected.
411.    Errors are transient return values the caller maps to abort-on-`?`; no error
412.    is part of the persistent abstract resource. Conflict conditions live in
413.    per-call `ensures` (`!all_free(R)`), not in `PhysModView`.
414. 
415. 5. **Make the `Err` arm of `init`/`book_*` promise full state preservation
416.    (`v' == v`).** Rejected as unsound: booking mutates the global incrementally
417.    and stops at the first conflict, so earlier regions stay booked. The code
418.    does not roll back; a `v' == v` ensures would be a false spec. We promise
419.    only `inv()` (and the conflict predicate), which is all any caller observes.
420. 
421. 6. **Represent reserved frames as a `Seq<int>` (ordered) instead of reusing
422.    `Set<int>` from `FrameAllocView`.** Rejected. Order of booking is explicitly
423.    *not* caller-observable (the analysis lists "ordering in which regions are
424.    iterated" as a non-breaking internal). Sets are the right abstraction and
425.    are already the established frame-View vocabulary.
426. 
427. ---
428. 
429. ## 8. Global-state modeling note (deferred to proof phase)
430. 
431. `init`/`book_*` take **no `self`**: they read and mutate the global singletons
432. `frame::INSTANCE` (+ `INSTANCE_INIT`) and the `PhysMemoryManager`/`Upool`
433. singletons. The `v -> v'` transitions in §4 are therefore not a literal
434. `old(self)`/`self` pair. They will be realized in the proof phase by a ghost
435. token whose invariant is exactly `PhysModView::inv()` and whose value is
436. `PhysModView`, with:
437. 
438. - `initialized`  ↔ `frame::INSTANCE_INIT`,
439. - `frames`       ↔ `frame::INSTANCE@` (the verified `View for Inner`, valid when
440.   `initialized`),
441. - `manager_ready`↔ the `PhysMemoryManager` singleton's init flag.
442. 
443. This is an *attachment* detail; the abstract View, `inv()`, and the transitions
444. above are the target the token machinery must satisfy and do not change. (Same
445. pattern the bump-allocator View used to defer its atomic-ghost token.)
446.

# Build Nanvix

Use this skill when the user asks to build, compile, format, lint, or spell-check Nanvix. This
covers all build-system operations exposed through the `z` utility.

## Prerequisites

- Development environment set up per `doc/setup.md`.
- A local cross-compilation toolchain (`toolchain/`).
- **Windows 11:** GNU Make on PATH, Windows Hypervisor Platform enabled,
  Developer Mode enabled, and Rust toolchain installed. See `doc/setup.md` for details.

## Windows Setup Summary

Before building on Windows, ensure:

1. **Windows Hypervisor Platform** is enabled (`Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName HypervisorPlatform -All`, then reboot).
2. **Developer Mode** is on (Settings > Privacy & Security > For developers).
3. **GNU Make** is on PATH (`winget install ezwinports.make`).
4. **Rust toolchain** is installed via `winget install Rustlang.Rustup`.
5. Repository was cloned with `git clone -c core.symlinks=true`.
6. Git hooks are installed: `./z.ps1 setup`.

## Building

### Preferred Build Commands (using `z` utility)

```bash
# Build everything with the local toolchain.
./z build -- all
```

### Building Individual Components

```bash
# Kernel only.
./z build -- kernel
# Nanvixd only.
./z build -- all-nanvixd
# UserVM only.
./z build -- all-uservm
```

### Build Parameters

Set these as environment variables or pass them after `--` in the `z` command:

| Parameter        | Values                   | Default         |
|------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| `MACHINE`        | `microvm`                | `microvm`       |
| `TARGET`         | `x86`                    | `x86`           |
| `RELEASE`        | `yes`, `no`              | `no`            |
| `LOG_LEVEL`      | `trace`, `debug`,        | `error`         |
|                  | `info`, `warn`,          |                 |
|                  | `error`, `panic`         |                 |
| `PROFILER`       | `yes`, `no`              | `no`            |
| `DEPLOYMENT_MODE`| `standalone`,            | `standalone`    |
|                  | `single-process`,        |                 |
|                  | `multi-process`, `l2`    |                 |

Example with custom parameters:

```bash
./z build -- all RELEASE=yes LOG_LEVEL=error
```

### Manual Build Variants

```bash
# Default debug build.
./z build -- all
# Release build.
./z build -- all RELEASE=yes LOG_LEVEL=panic
# For echo-breakdown benchmark.
./z build -- all RELEASE=yes LOG_LEVEL=panic TIMESTAMP_MSG=yes

+  `view_design.md` §4.2-§4.4 (e.g. helper Ok arms state `all_reserved(R)` rather than the
+  full `v' == v.frames.book_all(R)` transition; `init` Ok states the headline facts rather
+  than `seed(..).book_all(P).book_covered(M)`). These are **sound and caller-complete** (see
+  item 11) and the dropped clauses were either derivable or not caller-observed; the
+  composed-transition form is correctly deferred to the proof phase together with the
+  stateful `phys_view()` token (`view_design.md` §8). No weakening of a caller-relied-upon
+  guarantee. Acceptable.
+
+### 4. No tautological ensures — **PASS (with reasoning)**
+All three functions contain a `match result { Ok => <fact>, Err => true }`. Taken alone
+`Err(_) => true` is the flagged pattern, **but the error path is not vacuous**: each
+function additionally states `phys_view().inv()` (and the two helpers also
+`phys_view().initialized`) **unconditionally**, outside the match. So on `Err` the contract
+still guarantees `inv()` (+ `initialized` for helpers). The `Err => true` arm is the
+idiomatic residual of a success-only postcondition and is the **sound** choice for these
+`external_body` (trusted) helpers — strengthening a trusted `Err` arm (e.g. claiming
+`!all_free(R)`) would assert an unverified fact about the real body. Not a vacuous spec.
+**PASS.**
+
+### 5. No subsumed ensures — **PASS**
+- `init`: unconditional `inv()` is subsumed by `live()` *only on the Ok path*, but `inv()`
+  is the sole guarantee on the Err path, so it is required globally — not subsumable.
+- Helpers: `inv()` adds `frames.wf()` that `initialized` alone does not give; the Ok-arm
+  `all_reserved(..)` is not derivable from `inv()`. None subsumed. **PASS.**
+
+### 6. Error paths have meaningful ensures — **PASS**
+Match style is used (`Ok => ..., Err => ...`). Error paths carry real guarantees via the
+unconditional `inv()` / `initialized` clauses (item 4). `init`'s Err arm is intentionally
+`true` beyond `inv()` because the caller aborts on `?` and observes no partial state
+(`caller_analysis.md` L91-96, `view_design.md` §4.4 / §7.5 — explicitly justified). **PASS.**
+
+### 7. No assume_specification for workspace-internal code — **PASS**
+`make verify-kernel` cheating check: `assume=0`. Only external registration present is
+`ExLinkedList` (`#[verifier::external_type_specification]` for `alloc::collections::LinkedList`,
+a std type — `mod.spec.rs` L65-69). No `assume_specification` on any kernel-internal item. **PASS.**
+
+### 8. vstd searched before any assume_specification — **PASS (N/A)**
+No `assume_specification` used. `bugs.md` documents that `vstd` was searched for a
+`LinkedList` model and none exists (orphan rule blocks providing one downstream), which is
+why the two iterating helpers are `external_body` instead. **PASS.**
+
+### 9. Specs written for the caller — **PASS**
+`init`'s ensures are drop-in for the caller's proof: `live()` (single liveness fact downstream
+`virt::init` needs) and `all_reserved(..)` / MMIO-covered⇒reserved (the "booked ⇒ never
+allocated" safety property the caller writes directly). Helper specs are phrased in the same
+`FrameAllocView` vocabulary `init` consumes. **PASS.**
+
+### 10. Trait obligations — **PASS (none)**
+In-scope functions are free functions implementing no trait; no `Drop`/`Iterator`/`GlobalAlloc`
+contracts apply (`caller_analysis.md` "Trait Obligations: None"). **PASS.**
+
+### 11. Spec completeness (advisory) — **PASS (advisory)**
+No `spec-completeness` skill is installed in this repo; assessed manually. The only intentional
+nondeterminism is `init`'s `Err => true` arm, which **matches the caller expectation**
+(abort-on-`?`, no partial-state reliance). Ok arms fully pin the caller-observed post-state.
+Acceptable per the rule (intentional nondeterminism matching caller expectations). **PASS.**
+
+### 12. Loop invariants — **PASS**
+`book_physical_memory_regions` has a `for region in ...iter()` loop; `book_mmio_regions` has a
+`for` + an inner `while start < end` loop; `init` has no loops. The two looping functions are
+`#[verus_verify(external_body)]`, so Verus does not verify their bodies and does not require
+`invariant` clauses (and could not check them). No body-verified function in scope contains a
+loop. `make verify-kernel` reports `no_decreases=0`. **PASS.**
+
+### 13. No cheating on module's own functions — **PASS (reported + individually challenged)**
+Global counts (`make verify-kernel`): `assume=0 external_body=15 admit=2 trusted=0 cfg_gate=5`.
+In-scope (`mm::phys/mod.rs` + `mod.proof.rs`) items, each addressed individually:
+
+- `mod.rs:73 book_physical_memory_regions` — `external_body`. **Allowed**: listed in
+  `tcb-allowed.md` ("external_body introduced while speccing mm::phys") and root-caused in
+  `bugs.md` (no `vstd` `LinkedList` model; orphan rule forbids supplying one). Carries
+  meaningful `requires`/`ensures`. OK.
+- `mod.rs:103 book_mmio_regions` — `external_body`. **Allowed**: same `tcb-allowed.md` entry
+  and `bugs.md` rationale (LinkedList iteration). Carries meaningful `requires`/`ensures`. OK.
+- `mod.proof.rs:9 lemma_frame_initialized` — `admit()`. Asserts `phys_view().initialized &&
+  frames.wf()` after `frame::init`. I verified `frame::init` (frame.rs:657) is `external_body`
+  with **no `verus_spec`** (no ensures), and it is out of this module's scope (`tcb-allowed.md`
+  skip-list + "do not touch unlisted functions"). Therefore this fact cannot be derived in the
+  spec phase and cannot be supplied by adding a contract to the callee here. It is the
+  documented spec-phase stand-in for the external dependency's postcondition, to be discharged
+  by the ghost-token machinery in the proof phase (`view_design.md` §8, and the lemma's own
+  doc-comment). **Acceptable-deferred** (external-dependency contract, temporarily allowed).
+- `mod.proof.rs:22 lemma_manager_ready` — `admit()`. Same situation: `PhysMemoryManager::init`
+  (manager.rs:86) is `external_body` with no ensures and out of scope. **Acceptable-deferred.**

+`ExLinkedList`) are cross-module / external dependencies in other files, all enumerated in
+`tcb-allowed.md`, out of this module's scope. **PASS** (every in-scope cheating site
+individually accounted for; none removable within this phase/scope).

+`spec_drift.py check phys-mod` (baseline `f5a2b87` = specification phase-start SHA):

+`bugs.md` exists and is current: no code bugs in the three targets (logically correct, no

+- `make check-kernel` (build) → `{"reason":"build-finished","success":true}`, exit 0.
